answer.rationale: Constraints bind hard: 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer. Any action that introduces migration work inside that window (switch_primary_vendor) trades a certain delivery risk for an uncertain cost gain, and memory_c2 is silent on exactly the thing that matters here \u2014 it records fast onboarding and accurate invoicing under unstated (likely slacker) capacity conditions, not on-time performance at 94% utilization. add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right move for a constrained component but does not address the 18% spend mandate and consumes the one decision slot. defer_decision (memory_c5) worked for a non-critical service on month-to-month terms; this contract is critical and does not auto-renew, so deferring risks an uncovered supply gap. That leaves renewal-side options. Plain renew_incumbent (memory_c1) protects delivery but delivers no savings against the mandate. negotiate_terms is the only direction that plausibly serves both halves of the objective: it holds the existing integration and delivery schedule steady while attacking price, and memory_c4 records benchmarking moving the incumbent on price and payment terms. memory_c6 suggests a multi-year commitment as the lever that unlocks volume pricing, so that is the concession to offer \u2014 but it is also the risk I am flagging: locking in a long term purely to hit a one-year cost target can quietly narrow service scope, expedite rights, or flexibility in later cycles, and c6's claim that scope held may not transfer to a negotiation conducted under visible budget duress where the incumbent knows I cannot walk. I am verifying memory_c4 rather than c2 because c4 is the load-bearing memory for the action I intend: I need to know how much margin was actually recovered, whether the leverage came from a credible alternative supplier (which I do not currently have, given the delivery constraint) or from benchmarking alone, and whether 18% is even in reach. If the archive shows the recovery was small or depended on a walk-away threat I cannot make, my confidence in hitting the mandate this cycle drops and the honest output becomes a partial saving plus an explicit flag to finance rather than a claim of success. Running this as a standard negotiation, not a broad multi-year lock-in, keeps the term length open until c4 is read.
